=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:memory_force_tick_put, the clone-then-push path (~lines 710-810) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent phase-end calls can race through the clone/edit/push window and write conflicting ai-memory records.
  WHY: The clone-then-push path has no distributed lock or atomic replace, so the collision check only mitigates after the fact and can still lose or duplicate the record.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:_force_tick_latest_gate_tsv, lines ~120-155 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: A malformed cooldown timestamp silently fail-opens dispatch with no diagnostic.
  WHY: The ValueError handler clears candidate and age, prints false blank fields, and lets a corrupted ai-memory record disable cooldown invisibly.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:tracking-issue resolution block (lines ~160-290, _fetch_pull_request_json, _fetch_issue_body, regex fallbacks) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: GitHub API or JSON failures in tracking-issue resolution are treated as an empty result, so real force-tick events can be skipped silently.
  WHY: The PR/issue-body/regex fallbacks coerce errors to empty strings via `|| true`, so the caller only sees the generic skip message and loses the fast-follow tick on transient failures.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:_dispatch_integration_judge_now function (lines ~85-105) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The force-tick helper is wrapped in `|| true`, so dispatch failures are swallowed and the resolver can silently no-op.
  WHY: The original inline dispatch path logged specific failure modes, but the helper call now suppresses them and leaves the cron tick as the only fallback, adding latency.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:_force_tick_render_record_file, heredoc ~lines 340-370 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Malformed wrapper_json can still abort _force_tick_render_record_file before the record is persisted.
  WHY: Only the second json.loads is guarded; the first wrapper load can raise on a bad memory record under set -euo pipefail, losing idempotency state.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:_memory_force_tick_collision_wrapper and _latest(), lines ~547-580 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Re-enabled cooldown records can still be suppressed by stale last_attempted_timestamp handling.
  WHY: _latest still prefers last_attempted_timestamp for some disabled-record paths, so the collision wrapper does not always clear stale state after re-enable.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: memory_force_tick_put, the clone-then-push path (~lines 755-810)
  Problem: Two concurrent phase-end calls that both pass the collision-wrapper check before either pushes can both write a record (one push may be rejected by git, but the collision check does not use a distributed lock).
  Why it fails at runtime: Under normal 30-second cooldown the window is narrow, but when two distinct phase-end events fire against the same tracking issue within the same clone-to-push window (e.g., review-blocked and validation-finalized both completing at once), one dispatch may slip past the cooldown. The peer re-read path in orchestrate_force_tick.sh partially mitigates this for the dispatch case, but the record on the ai-memory branch can end up with the loser's timestamp, making the next cooldown check use a timestamp from a dispatch that was suppressed.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh
  Line or code reference: _force_tick_latest_gate_tsv, lines ~120-155
  Problem: When the cooldown record's timestamp field is malformed (not valid ISO-8601), the ValueError handler sets candidate="" and age="" which causes the function to print "false\t\t" — the caller interprets empty fields as "cooldown not active" and dispatches.
  Why it fails at runtime: This is correct fail-open behavior but the absence of any log warning means a corrupted ai-memory record silently disables cooldown for that tracking issue.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: memory_force_tick_put (the git clone/cp/commit/push path around lines 710-800)
  Problem: No distributed lock or atomic replace mechanism exists on the ai-memory branch. Two concurrent phase-end calls (e.g., review + validate finalization for the same tracking issue) can race through the clone/edit/push window, causing one to overwrite or duplicate the other's record.
  Why it fails at runtime: The "another run already claimed the cooldown window" re-read path only mitigates after the fact. The window between clone and push is unprotected. The existing test `test_memory_force_tick_put_refuses_same_window_overwrite_for_new_attempt` only exercises the collision wrapper in isolation, not the real branch race condition.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh
  Line or code reference: tracking-issue resolution block (lines ~260-290) and the three gh/api calls that feed it
  Problem: All three fallback paths (`_force_tick_fetch_pull_request_json`, `_force_tick_fetch_issue_body`, and regex parsing) treat API failures or malformed JSON as empty strings via `|| true`, silently falling through to the generic "No tracking issue resolved for force-tick dispatch; skipping." message.
  Why it fails at runtime: On transient GitHub API flakes (rate limit, network timeout, permission errors), a real orchestrator phase-end event produces no poll tick. The only log message is the generic skip message with no indication that an API failure occurred. This defeats the "fast-follow tick" intent of S3.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
  Line or code reference: _dispatch_integration_judge_now function (lines ~85-105)
  Problem: The helper call is unconditionally wrapped with `|| true`, so the script continues even if the force-tick helper fails or is missing. The original inline dispatch logic had explicit warning logs for each failure mode (GH_PAT missing, workflow name unknown, dispatch failure).
  Why it fails at runtime: Resolver bail events that previously had an explicit immediate dispatch with detailed logging now rely on a best-effort helper that can silently no-op. The cron tick becomes the fallback, adding up to 5 minutes of latency.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "Tests cover cooldown/no-op behavior and the dispatch payload shape."
  Expected change site: tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py (already present) + wiring into CI allowlist so the contract test actually runs
  Evidence of absence: The test file exists and covers the required behaviors, but it is not referenced in the explicit `python3 tests/<file>.py` allowlist in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and mirrored release workflows). Running `grep "test_orchestrate_force_tick" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns no matches. The test therefore does not execute in CI; coverage can regress silently.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Mirror the workflow edits into workflow-templates/ (§14)" and "Keep the matching listed workflow-template wrappers in sync where this issue already names them."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/ai-implement.yml, workflow-templates/ai-review.yml, workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml
  Evidence of absence: No diff hunk in the PR touches any workflow-templates/ file. However, these are thin `uses: shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/.github/workflows/...@stable` delegates that inherit changes from upstream automatically. The @stable mechanism satisfies the "stay in sync" requirement without manual wrapper edits.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2 (not an actual gap - @stable mechanism handles sync)
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh
  Line or code reference: _force_tick_render_record_file (heredoc ~lines 340-370)
  Problem: Two json.loads calls (for wrapper_json and payload_json) wrapped only in try/except on the second call; the first wrapper load can still raise on malformed memory record from get/put.
  Why it fails at runtime: set -euo pipefail aborts before persisting claim or final record, losing idempotency state for the tracking issue; reproduced in test_force_tick_records_dispatch_failure_status when gh workflow run fails.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  Line or code reference: _memory_force_tick_collision_wrapper (~lines 547-580) and _latest()
  Problem: _latest still prefers last_attempted_timestamp even for disabled records in some paths; collision_wrapper does not always suppress disabled state correctly after re-enable (test shows partial fix only).
  Why it fails at runtime: Re-enabled runs after FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false can be suppressed by stale attempted timestamp
